question:
The determinant $D=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & p\\1 & 2 & 1\\p & 1 & 2\end{vmatrix}$ has the value $4$.

(a) Expand $D$ and form an equation in $p$.

(b) Determine all possible real values of $p$.

(c) For each value of $p$, evaluate $\begin{vmatrix}2 & p\\p & 2\end{vmatrix}$ and compare the results.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=2\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 2\end{vmatrix}-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\p & 2\end{vmatrix}+p\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\p & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$D=2(4-1)-(2-p)+p(1-2p)$$
$$D=6-2+p+p-2p^2=4+2p-2p^2$$
Since $D=4$,
$$4+2p-2p^2=4$$
$$2p(1-p)=0$$

(b)
From $2p(1-p)=0$,
$$p=0\quad\text{or}\quad p=1$$

(c)
Let
$$E=\begin{vmatrix}2 & p\\p & 2\end{vmatrix}=4-p^2$$
For $p=0$,
$$E=4$$
For $p=1$,
$$E=3$$
Therefore, the corresponding determinant values are $4$ and $3$, and the first is greater than the second by $1$.

options.A:
(a) $D=4+2p+2p^2$, so $2p(1+p)=0$
(b) $p=0,-1$
(c) The corresponding determinants are $4$ and $3$
options.B:
(a) $D=4+2p-2p^2$, so $2p(1-p)=0$
(b) $p=0,1$
(c) The corresponding determinants are $4$ and $3$, and the first is greater by $1$
options.D:
(a) $D=4+2p-2p^2$, so $p(1-p)=4$
(b) $p=-1,2$
(c) The corresponding determinants are $3$ and $0$
